title: Bacterial Nucleic Acid Extraction Protocol Adapted for a Resource-Limited Setting
author: Bonie Datul

steps.title: Inoculate bacteria and grow culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate a loopful of bacteria into 5 mL Nutrient Broth and incubate overnight at room temperature with shaking.

steps.title: Transfer culture aliquot
steps.instruction: Transfer 1.5 mL of the overnight culture into a sterile 1.5‑mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 12 000 rpm (temperature not specified) for 3 min (00:03:00). Carefully discard the supernatant, leaving the cell pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bacterial pellet with 150 µL Resuspension Buffer, pipetting up and down vigorously, then incubate at 37 °C for 15 min (00:15:00).

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to the suspension, vortex to mix, then incubate at 65 °C for 20 min (00:20:00) vortexing gently every 5 min. If the lysate is not clear, extend incubation to 30 min or until clarified.

steps.title: Add NaCl and mix
steps.instruction: Cool the lysate to room temperature, add 35.0 µL of 5 M NaCl (giving an approximate final concentration of 0.5 M), and mix thoroughly by inverting the tube 10–20 times or vortexing gently for 5 s to avoid DNA shearing.

steps.title: Incubate on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture on ice for 10 min (00:10:00).

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 rpm (temperature not specified) for 3 min (00:03:00). A white pellet of protein and cell debris should be visible; if not, place the tube on ice for 5–10 min and re‑centrifuge.

steps.title: Transfer DNA‑containing supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer 250 µL of the clear supernatant to a new clean 1.5‑mL tube, avoiding any of the white pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation wash 1
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL cold 70 % ethanol, invert gently a few times to wash the DNA, then centrifuge at 14 000 rpm for 3 min (00:03:00) (use 4 °C if available).

steps.title: Remove ethanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pour off or pipette out the supernatant without disturbing the loose DNA pellet.

steps.title: Repeat ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol addition, gentle inversion, and centrifugation (steps 10–11) once more.

steps.title: Final ethanol removal
steps.instruction: After the last wash, remove as much remaining ethanol as possible with a fine‑tipped pipette; leaving a small amount is acceptable to avoid losing the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet at room temperature in a laminar flow hood with the fan on for 10–20 min (00:10:00‑00:20:00) **or** in a dry bath/heat block at 37 °C for 5–10 min (00:05:00‑00:10:00) until all visible ethanol has evaporated. Do not over‑dry.

steps.title: Preheat TE buffer
steps.instruction: Preheat 1× TE buffer (pH 8.0) at 65 °C for 10 min (00:10:00).

steps.title: Re‑suspend DNA in TE
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 µL of the preheated TE buffer to the dried DNA pellet.

steps.title: Gentle resuspension
steps.instruction: Tap or flick the tube gently to dissolve the DNA; avoid vigorous vortexing which can shear long DNA molecules.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Store the DNA solution at 4 °C for short‑term use or at –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Optional: repeat low‑yield steps
steps.instruction: If cell yield is low, repeat the inoculation (step 1) and transfer (step 2) to obtain more material.

steps.title: Optional RNase treatment
steps.instruction: Add 5.0 µL RNase A (10 mg/mL) to the suspension, vortex, and incubate at 37 °C for 15 min (00:15:00).

steps.title: Optional lysis and incubation
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL freshly prepared lysis buffer, vortex vigorously, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min (00:30:00).

steps.title: Optional ice incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate on ice for 30 min (00:30:00) or longer (e.g., overnight at –20 °C) to enhance DNA precipitation.

steps.title: Optional ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL ice‑cold absolute ethanol, invert slowly until DNA strings become visible (often fine white threads). This may require several inversions. Pause point: samples can be stored at –20 °C before proceeding.

steps.title: Optional pellet centrifugation
steps.instruction: Invert gently a few times, then centrifuge at 14 000 rpm for 3 min (00:03:00). A visible white DNA pellet should form at the bottom or side of the tube.

steps.title: Optional DNA elution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5 000 rpm for 10 s (00:00:10) to collect the eluted DNA solution at the bottom of the tube.
